Saves and world files

Your world file keeps your character, carried items and changes to the world. Untouched terrain is rebuilt from the saved seed and generation. Display, audio and input preferences are shared across worlds.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents

  3. Save limits

  5. Opening the game
  6. How this was checked

What a save keeps

Saving writes the whole world file. It keeps:

  • Your position, view direction and game mode (creative or survival).
  • In survival: health, hunger, thirst and stamina. A legacy temperature value is retained for compatibility and has no gameplay effect.
  • Your inventory, hotbar bindings and selected slot, and the tool you hold.
  • Every block you changed, including water and door state.
  • Time of day, weather and season controls.
  • Your home crate and rest point, chest contents and one saved build palette.
  • Placed furniture with its stored items, whether each lamp is switched on, and a stove's contents and unfinished batch.
  • Journal places, expedition finds, milestones and the map destination.
  • Up to 8 sailing boats.
  • Player-hatched animals and dropped item stacks. What a world save keeps

Procedural wildlife, flying projectiles and primed TNT are not saved. Temporary diagnostic overlays also reset. Display, audio and input preferences are shared separately; a world file still contains older settings fields for compatibility.

When the game saves

  • F6 saves now. “World saved safely” appears only after the world file is written, including the world you host. In a world you joined, or a session started with --no-save, F6 writes nothing and says “This session does not save the world locally”.
  • Autosave checks about every 30 seconds and saves when world state has changed.
  • Choosing Main menu, Save & quit or Quit, pressing Ctrl+Q, closing the window, or loading or creating another world saves first.
  • Main menu keeps a hosted world running. Use Stop hosting on the Multiplayer page to end hosting.

A failed save shows “Save refused:” with the reason and keeps a visible warning until a save succeeds. If saving fails while you are quitting, the game stays open so you can fix the problem and retry. Saving: autosave, F6 and quitting safely

If you save while sitting or lying in a bed, the world reopens with you standing beside it. Saving needs a clear spot to stand there; otherwise it is refused with 'Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player' or 'Seat exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player'. Make room and save again.

In a world you joined, the server keeps the world. A dedicated server confirms most actions only after it has saved them; see Multiplayer and feature limits.

If a stopped host cannot recover your pack

  1. Keep the session open. If the save before stopping failed, the world is still hosted; fix the reported problem and try Stop hosting again.
  2. If hosting has stopped and pack recovery is blocked, press F6 to retry. Continue returns to the repair session so you can adjust conflicting Creative catalogue choices.
  3. Press Shift+F6 to open the recovery choice. Keep current choices (or Esc) changes nothing. To accept the host's final state, hold Hold: use final pack for 3 seconds with the mouse, Enter or Space: your pack and mode become the host's final ones, and conflicting Creative catalogue choices are set aside; your hotbar, tools and map pins stay as they are. If the final world or pack is unavailable, the choice is Use last saved world instead, also held for 3 seconds: the last saved world and its matching pack come back together, and later hosted changes are set aside.
  4. Before switching, the game saves a separate recovery copy, with a RECOVERY.txt, in a pack-recovery-copies folder next to the world's save file, and names it on screen; keep it. If that copy cannot be written, your current choices stay as they are and the session stays open; follow the reported error before choosing again with Shift+F6.
Careful. An unresolved pack blocks ordinary saving, world replacement and quitting. Recovery files next to the save belong to the unfinished recovery; do not delete them to get past the choice. The dialog explains which later state will be set aside. Multiplayer menu: Host this world (LAN hosting)

Save limits

  • Each world file is capped at 8 MiB. A save that would be bigger is refused with “Save refused: refusing to exceed the 8 MiB debug-save safety budget”, and the existing file stays as it was.
  • A world holds up to 200,000 changed blocks. Beyond that, new building is refused with 'Save edit budget reached'. Spreading water never pushes a save past the limit.
  • From 190,000 changed blocks, the status line warns 'saving stops at 200000' about every 20 seconds.
  • A home crate, blueprint or structure that would go past the limit is not placed.
  • On a hosted or dedicated server, the size cap also limits other actions, such as crafting, hitting animals, moving or dropping items and filling flasks. If the world file would go over, the server refuses with a message ending 'would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid', for example 'Crafting would exceed the save budget or saved state is invalid'. An exact fit is allowed, and actions that make the save smaller still work.

Make and reopen a backup

  1. Open Worlds, select a saved world and choose Create backup or press Ctrl+B. Stop hosting first if this is the hosted world.
  2. Wait for Backup ready and keep the location shown. A completed backup ends in backups/backup-<time>-<process>-<sequence>/snapshot/. The active local world is saved before copying.
  3. To reopen a backup, close the game and copy the whole completed snapshot folder into a new folder such as worlds/recovered-house/. Keep the original world and the backup.
  4. Start the game and open the new copy from Worlds. A .pending folder is an unfinished attempt, not a completed backup.

Backups contain the save and its available name, preview and session-history files. They are stored beside worlds, so deleting the source world does not delete the backup. Finish any outstanding save recovery before making an ordinary backup or duplicate. Create and reopen a world backup World size limits

Older and newer saves

  • A world keeps the terrain generation it was created with. Create world defaults to generation 12 and also offers older generations; loading or updating a world preserves its saved choice. World generations (terrain rule versions)
  • A world saved before the half-metre block grid is refused with 'world predates the half-metre voxel grid; a new world is required'. Create a new world instead.
  • A world saved by a newer version of the game is refused by an older one with 'world was saved by a newer version of voxelgame'. Update the game to open it.
  • A file that is not a Voxelgame save is refused with 'not a voxelgame save'.

If a world will not open, read When a world cannot be loaded. Older and newer saves

Opening the game

  • Only one copy of the game runs per user. Opening it again brings the open window to the front and shows 'qiqi was already open; click the world to recapture the mouse'. Opening the game twice
  • When the game first opens, a tumbling wireframe cube settles into the qiqi logo above the current loading stage and an activity bar. Later world loads show only the stage and the bar. There is no percentage. Loading screen

How this guide was checked

What a save keeps comes from the save writer's section list (crates/voxelgame-core/src/save/write.rs) and the session-only settings in the ledger. Limits and messages were checked against Voxelgame 51169272: 8 MiB and 200,000-edit constants and the 190,000 warning threshold (save.rs, game.rs), the 'saves' refusals and the version checks (save.rs, load.rs). Opening rules come from src/app.rs and src/single_instance.rs. Targeted compatibility clarification at 35cfc2f8: the serialized temperature field remains inert in survival.rs; other save evidence retains its original audit. Targeted 5 November source follow-up at aa136e0103ce5599c6d8a9f70c669dbc758b7357: current save sections, shared preferences, generation 12, Worlds backup/recovery and stopped-host retry/choice paths. Existing unrelated opening-screen evidence keeps its earlier check. The game’s dated WORLD_BACKUP_20261016 verification records offscreen backup recovery; it was not rerun for this guide. Targeted 8 November 2026 source follow-up at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c: F6 confirms only after a local write (src/app.rs), the 8 MiB refusal in the save encoder and writer (save.rs), size refusals on servers (session/crafting.rs, creatures.rs, items.rs, water.rs and home/*.rs), dedicated-server save waits (voxelgame-server host/furniture/durability/stock.rs), the seat and bed exit check before saving (save/write.rs, game/furniture/resting.rs, seating.rs) and saved lamp and stove state (furniture/lamp_state.rs, furniture/cooking.rs). The stopped-host recovery steps were re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480: voxelgame-render startup_ui/stopped_owner_choice.rs:16-61; voxelgame-core game/stopped_owner_choice.rs:132-230; src/net_client/ready_recovery/canonical_choice.rs:50-164; src/app.rs:1097-1108. Opening-screen messages, limits, version refusals, autosave and the Create backup path were re-checked on 8 November 2026 at Voxelgame c56a00c4219e69c433f2bb6f908198998519fdfc: src/app.rs:79-85,1543-1562,1634-1650,1838-1846,1992-2027; crates/voxelgame-core/src/save.rs:107-120,318-326; save/load.rs:31-50; src/app/backup.rs:13-47; src/world_backup.rs:14-44.

Initial ledger audit: Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; article updated 8 November 2026. Source-checked in this follow-up; no new game process, native save/fault injection, LAN play or screenshot capture. Existing loading-screen prose retains its earlier audit. No game run has checked these backup and stopped-host steps. A session that has not been saved is not guaranteed to survive a restart.
